newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: NZ firm forms Cambodian air service joint venture.
newsitem.headline: NZ firm forms Cambodian air service joint venture.

text.p: New Zealand-based Helicopters (NZ) Ltd has formed a joint venture with Royal Air Cambodge to provide helicopter and small airplane service in Cambodia, company officials said on Wednesday.

Brian McDonald, chief executive of Helicopters (NZ), said the venture, called Royal Air Services, would begin operations in one month with aerial survey work for mineral exploration companies operating in Cambodia.
He told Reuters that Royal Air Services had brought one AS350B helicopter to Phnom Penh and would bring in more helicopters and small fixed wing charter aircraft as dictated by market demand.

Royal Air Services will focus on the mineral and off-shore oil exporation markets, as well as charter flights for tourism and cargo and medical evacuation service, McDonald said, declining to provide details on the value of the deal.
Royal Air Cambodge Chairman Vichit Ith said his airline held a 60 percent stake in the venture and Helicopters (NZ) held a 40 percent share.
Royal Air Cambodge is a joint venture between Malaysia Helicopter Services and the Cambodian government. It holds a monopoly on all domestic cargo and passenger operations.
